A-07 Events (matches)

Bangla name: ইভেন্ট (ম্যাচ)

← 10 · Admin portal · Contents · Open queries

1. Name and purpose

Events. An event is one match or show of a program at a venue, made of one or more segments (a sport segment with two teams, or a concert segment). Creating an event builds its own copy of the commercial settings and of the venue's levels with prices and capacities, so ticket sales run per event. Publishing makes it visible and sellable; the platform then also tells app users by push notification. Concepts: shared database, Redis live capacity.

2. Trigger and actor

Staff with roles admin, event_manager, ticket_manager, ticket_operator (BCBPersonnel) (class attribute of EventsController; [AuthorizeProgram] is commented out). Entry: program menu Events (/events): list, Create (/events/create), Edit (/events/edit/:id), Details (/events/event-details/:id).

3. Business flow

  1. List events of the selected program; filter, search.
  2. Create: program, venue, name (≤ 60 characters), start and end, cover image, one or more segments (name, type Sport or Concert, start, end, team 1 and team 2 for sport, banner image).
  3. Review and adjust prices, capacity, settings (A-08, A-09, A-10).
  4. Publish (needs published ticket layouts for all active galleries, A-13); customers can then see and, once selling opens, buy.
  5. Toggle active/inactive a published event; Unpublish only before selling starts; Duplicate; Delete.

4. Technical flow

  1. Create [HTTP + user token] POST /admin/api/v1/events (multipart/form-data, CreateEvent). EventManager.CreateAsync: - CheckValidityOfCreateEvent: program and venue ids exist; name required and ≤ 60; start not in the past; end after start; cover image required; per segment: name, dates, banner required; sport needs two different teams, concert gets no teams. - A new EventId GUID is assigned to the event and to each segment. - The program settings are copied into a new EventSettings row (limits, selling hours, prefix, VAT, service charge, gateway) (A-03); IsVatInclusive is also set on the event. - Insert; upload the cover to eventcover/{id}/... and each banner to eventsegmentcover/... (X-20). - GenerateEventVenueDetails(programId, eventId) copies the program's venue-detail rows into the event (A-09). - [HTTP + user token] IBookingClient.CreateCapacity(list) creates a Capacities row per level in Booking (TicketingCapacity = the level's seating capacity, seats if any), then GetEventLiveCapacity seeds event_live:{id} in Redis (S-02).
  2. Update PUT /admin/api/v1/events/{id} (multipart): - Not published: CheckValidityOfUpdateEvent (venue exists, name, dates, segment rules incl. "Concert segments cannot have team IDs."), then the event and its segments are updated. - Published: the validity check is skipped and only these fields change: event end time, VAT-inclusive flag, cover image, each segment's end time, banner and teams. - The caches event_details:*, admin_event_details:*, event_settings_details:{id}, event_venue_details:* are deleted.
  3. Publish PUT /admin/api/v1/events/publish/{id}: fails if already published, if the program has no ticket layout for the venue ("No ticket layout configuration found for VenueId: n."), or if an active gallery has no published layout ("Ticket layout is not configured for all active galleries."); sets IsPublished, clears the same caches, resets event_ticket_counter:{eventId} to 0, and sends a push notification to all app users (title "New Event Available!", data eventId, eventName, type = event_published) through PushNotification; a failed push is logged and ignored (X-23).
  4. Unpublish PUT .../unpublish/{id}: fails if not published, or if event start − TicketSellingStartFromHour is already in the past ("Event can't unpublished after start ticket selling."); clears caches.
  5. Toggle PUT .../toggle-status/{id}: only for published events, flips IsActive; clears caches.
  6. Duplicate POST .../duplicate/{id}: creates "{name} - Copy" unpublished, copies segments, settings, venue details and capacities (again through CreateCapacity and GetEventLiveCapacity), and the gate and checker assignments of the original (A-18).
  7. Delete DELETE .../{id}: soft delete (IsDeleted), clears the list cache.
  8. Date-times such as TicketSellingStartDateTime, TicketSellingStopDateTime and TicketAvailabilityStartDateTime are computed when events are read (event start/end minus the settings' hours; event settings if present, else program settings), not stored.

7. Data and side effects

New event, segments, settings copy, venue-detail copy, Booking capacities, Redis counters, S3 images, and on publish a push to all devices. Activity log entries (X-24).

9. Handover notes

  1. Creation is not atomic across services. The event is saved first; the Booking CreateCapacity call happens afterwards over HTTP. If it fails, the event exists without capacity rows, and the API returns an error, so a retry creates a second event. Check Booking Capacity rows when an event "has no seats" (S-01).
  2. A published event skips validation on update, so its end time can be set before its start time, and the segment end can be changed without checks (only end times and teams are accepted for published events).
  3. Settings are a copy taken at creation. Later changes to the program settings do not reach existing events; use A-08.
  4. Null end date. EndDateTime is nullable in the DTO, the create check does not reject a null end, but the date computation dereferences EndDateTime.Value; always send an end time.
  5. Start in the past is rejected on every update, even of a draft: editing a draft event after its start time fails with "StartDateTime must be greater than or equal to the current date and time."
  6. Unpublish is only possible before selling opens; after that, use Toggle (inactive) to stop sales.
  7. Duplicate copies gate and checker assignments of the original event, so check them before publishing the copy.
  8. Publish sends a push to everyone and there is no preview or test mode, so a test publish in production notifies real users.
